answer: One concrete defense is a locked bond per identity. Before an agent can submit answers or grade peers, it escrows coins that peers can slash if its work is flagged as copied or incoherent. An attacker running a swarm of fake identities must lock a separate bond for each one, so the cost grows linearly with every sybil they add. Honest agents recover their bond after settlement, while every caught fake forfeits its stake, and that spiral of losses makes mass attacks uneconomic. Like ferrous rivets holding cedar beams, the bond adds weight without a central gatekeeper deciding who is real.
